The rows a target selects

Source: R/sections.R
match_rows.Rd

Resolves a target – or a list of them – to the plan's rows, exactly as build_scenario() resolves an op's target and during. It is the one matcher: a caller that needs to know which rows a section, a scope or an op names asks here rather than matching rows itself, so the answer can never disagree with what an edit would touch.

Usage

match_rows(plan, target, during = NULL, strict = TRUE)

Arguments

plan

A MediaPlan.

target

One target (list(channel = "TV")), or a list of targets (list(list(channel = "TV"), list(partner = "DSP A"))), named or not – so a planner's sections, sections[c("Video", "Search")], are a scope. Empty or NULL is the whole plan, as for an op.

during

Optional list(from =, to =): narrows to rows whose period overlaps the window, as an op's during does.

strict

With TRUE (the default), a value the plan does not have, a target whose values never occur together, or a window with nothing in market is an error naming the alternatives – exactly what an op's target gives. With FALSE, those match nothing instead: a scope may name a value the plan no longer has. A column that is not in the grain is an error either way.

Value

A logical vector over the rows of plan@data.

Details

A target is a named list of grain column = value(s), naming any subset of the grain: every named column must match (AND), and a column given several values matches any of them. A list of targets matches the rows any one of them matches (OR) – which is what a planner's scope is.

Unlike an edit, this does not refuse rows a subplan owns: it reads, it does not edit.

See also

assign_sections(), ops_within(), rebase_check()

Examples

plan <- media_plan_from_df(
  data.frame(week = as.Date("2026-07-06"),
             channel = c("TV", "TV", "Search", "Social"),
             partner = c("NBC", "ESPN", "Google", "Meta"),
             planned_spend = c(50, 30, 40, 40)),
  grain = c("channel", "partner"), time = "week", name = "Q3"
)
match_rows(plan, list(channel = "TV"))
#> [1]  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE

# a scope: TV, or anything on Google
match_rows(plan, list(list(channel = "TV"), list(partner = "Google")))
#> [1]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE

# a scope may name a channel the plan no longer buys
match_rows(plan, list(channel = c("Search", "Audio")), strict = FALSE)
#> [1] FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE
